fact: Officials cite the Government Enterprise Service Bus (GovESB) as the backbone for secure data exchange across ministries, and the e-Government Authority's Director General urges institutions to ensure systems are connected through it; no count of connected systems or figure for its traffic is given.
source_slug: 2026-01-26 Tanzania's GovTech success raises bar for East Africa's digital states

fact: The Prime Minister ordered all public institutions to join GovESB, built by e-GA so government systems can read each other and exchange information, by 30 July 2025, saying joining is free.

On 17 October 2024 the Prime Minister said the government was continuing with the Jamii X-Change system so that government systems read each other, and the ICT minister said his ministry was still coordinating its construction.

On 27 August 2024 the ministry's permanent secretary said the ministry and the e-Government Authority were still building Jamii X-Change, funded through the Digital Tanzania project, to let sectoral ICT systems read each other and exchange data.

The e-Government Authority's roadmap states that the Government Data Sharing and Exchange Platform, GovESB, was established and that public institutions use it to exchange information between them; it also says the e-Government Act 2019 requires all government systems to exchange data through it.
NIDA states Jamii X-Change, its X-Road-based secure data exchange platform, is operational, with Zan X-Change in testing and Revenue X-Change under implementation.
e-GA says its GovESB links public bodies' ICT systems so they exchange data, and 109 public institutions are connected.
e-GA says 109 public institutions are connected to GovESB and 117 systems registered, including NIDA, BRELLA, NECTA, the Judiciary, Police, TAKUKURU and NPS.
The article says GovESB, the Government Enterprise Service Bus developed by e-GA as the common exchange layer, provides the infrastructure through which separate government systems exchange data.
